d.x: Got yr card. Problem is: don't have yr address! Wd love to see you. Write w/number! xo Jeremy.

d.g: A letter of the Anglo-Saxon runic alphabet, ᚣ, representing the vowel sounds /y/ and /yː/ in Old English.

yr.e: Learned borrowing from Old English ȳr, the literal translation of which is uncertain: perhaps “yew” or “bow (made of yew)”, based on Old Norse ýr.
